SELECTED_INDEX: 5
CONFIDENCE: 0.7
EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows a strong ester carbonyl near 1737 cm⁻¹ and a very strong C=C band at 1651 cm⁻¹, consistent with an α,β-unsaturated ester. Multiple vinylic C–H stretches (3022 and 3098 cm⁻¹) and prominent C–H stretches in the 2900–3100 cm⁻¹ region (GFQ-003) support an alkene with sp² C–H. The bands at 1294 and 1057 cm⁻¹ fit C–O stretching from an ester and an alcohol, respectively—unique to candidate 5 among the unsaturated esters here. Vinylic out-of-plane C–H wags around 953–995–872 cm⁻¹ are compatible with a disubstituted alkene. The absence of an aldehydic C–H doublet (~2720/2820 cm⁻¹) disfavors formate/aldehyde candidates (2, 7); lack of an N–H stretch (~3300 cm⁻¹) rules out the amide (9); and the thioester (3), nitroalkene (10), and acid (6) are inconsistent with the observed carbonyl position and/or missing signature bands.
